articles.title: Massive fire erupts in jet fuel unit at Chevron's LA refinery
articles.content: STORY: A massive fire erupted at Chevron’s El Segundo refinery near Los Angeles on Thursday.Chevron said there were no injuries and all workers were accounted for…But it did raise questions over fuel supply in California, an isolated energy market. The fire broke out in a jet fuel production unit, which supplies the Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).It’s not immediately clear how it started. A source said it was also unclear if the incident had impacted the refinery’s ability to produce fuel - or whether fuel already stored there was affected. Tamara Smith, a local resident, said it was a scary moment.“I heard a little explosion. It sounded like the start of a 3.0 earthquake. And then a second later, there was another loud explosion, and it felt like a 5. It’s Chevron's second biggest refinery in the U.S.; it supplies a fifth of all motor vehicle fuels and 40% of the jet fuel consumed in southern California.Analysts said it’s unlikely to impact wider oil prices, but due to isolation from other refining centers, the state’s gasoline prices could rise.In addition to Chevron, state and federal safety agencies will investigate the fire after the blaze is extinguished.
